text:
Maria D.: heads up — we saw another short spike in request queues hitting 95% of GPU pool capacity in eu-west-1 around 08:12 UTC. latency SLOs tripped for ~90s and a bunch of requests got soft-shed. stacktrace looks like admission denial + retries piling up in front-end.
Jon: ugh. was that the same customer traffic pattern as yesterday (short fanout of ~600 small chat requests)?
Maria D.: yep, similar burst profile. warm-pool had 0 available and prewarm didn't kick fast enough. warm_pool_grace currently 10s, prealloc_cooldown 30s.
Sasha: can we increase warm_pool_grace + add a debounce on admit to avoid oscillation? right now admission controller scales up aggressively then immediately drops back when queue drains for 1s.
Kevin: +1. propose: warm_pool_grace=40s, prealloc_cooldown=90s, admission_debounce_ms=3000. also limit fast-scaling ramp to +25% per step to avoid cold starts overload.
Priya: cost note — moving grace to 40s will hold more GPUs idle; estimate +8% monthly for eu-west-1. ok if we do canary for 24h and measure blocked requests vs cost.
Maria D.: agreed on canary. plan: roll config to a small subset (pool-id: gfx-eu-preempt-2) at 09:30 UTC, monitor queue_length, p95 latency, and soft-shed count. rollback if soft-shed > 1% or p95 > 250ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
Jon: can we instead try admission token-bucket tweak first? increase burst tokens from 200 -> 350 and add a short hedging window to allow in-flight KV cache prep. Might reduce prewarm churn and cost.
Sasha: token-bucket is worth trying, but token bursts alone can still overload if no prewarmed GPUs. I'd rather combine token-burst bump + longer warm_pool_grace.
Kevin: I drafted a quick config snippet for the rollout. please review:
```
service.pool_defaults:
  warm_pool_grace: 40s
  prealloc_cooldown: 90s
  admission:
    debounce_ms: 3000
    token_bucket:
      capacity: 350
      refill_rate_per_sec: 50
  scale_step_limit_pct: 25
```
Priya: looks fine. schedule note: make sure dedicated capacity autopruning doesn't fight this. there was an autopruning policy in the account that reclaimed GPUs after 60s idle. that'll negate the grace change unless we change that too.
Maria D.: good catch — that autoprun is for non-critical pools. we'll add an override for canary pool.
ops-bot: CHANGE_REQUEST opened by Maria D. for pool gfx-eu-preempt-2 -> adding warm_pool_grace override, token bucket, and debounce. Request ID: CR-2026-443.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled at 09:30 UTC to 10% of traffic for pool gfx-eu-preempt-2. Health checks: queue_length, soft_shed_count, p95_latency.
Jon: monitoring dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/pool/gfx-eu-preempt-2 and a short runbook snippet below to abort quickly:
```
if soft_shed_count > 0.01 * total_requests for 3m -> rollback CR-2026-443
if p95_latency > 250ms for 3m -> rollback
if cost_delta > +12% over 1h -> alert finance and revert
```
Sasha: I'll be on pager during the canary. if we see queue tail latency spike but no soft-shed, we can lower admission refill_rate to smooth things.
Priya: please post a short post-mortem in #postmortems if we hit >1% customers impacted. otherwise just close CR with notes.
Maria D.: thanks all. starting the canary plan and will post updates. :thumbsup:
